<blockquote>
<ul class="contains-task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" id="" disabled="" class="task-list-item-checkbox" aria-label="Incomplete task">  Find a solution for the comments on wordpress</li>
</ul>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">For new comments: Considering the following:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>The rewrite website is static</li>
<li>We do not have a mailing list</li>
<li>GitHub discussions is already being used</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">For every existing/new blog post, open a GitHub discussion and add a link to it<br>
on the relevant post.  Example: "Comment on $url".</p>
<p dir="auto">The main disadvantage is that, unlike Wordpress, this requires an account<br>
(i.e.: on GitHub) to comment.  Commenting without accounts might be possible<br>
with third-party embeds, such as Disqus, though personally I'd prefer to avoid<br>
more dependencies on such services.</p>
<p dir="auto">Sort of relevant discussion: <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="3505678" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/netblue30/firejail/discussions/4456" data-hovercard-type="discussion" data-hovercard-url="/netblue30/firejail/discussions/4456/hovercard" href="https://github.com/netblue30/firejail/discussions/4456">#4456</a>.</p>
<p dir="auto">After this, make the Wordpress comment section read-only/delete-only.</p>
<p dir="auto">Then, for every existing comment on the Wordpress site:</p>
<p dir="auto">Copy the author/date/content into a new comment in the relevant discussion.</p>
<p dir="auto">Now that I think about it, this would be one very useful use case for GitHub<br>
discussions.  If there was an easy way to embed them just like with other<br>
commenting platforms, I'm sure many software projects would use it.  I'd still<br>
consider self-hosting and etc to be better in most cases, but if a project is<br>
going to offload the costs to somebody else anyways...</p>
<blockquote>
<ul class="contains-task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" id="" disabled="" class="task-list-item-checkbox" aria-label="Incomplete task">  Push it to <code class="notranslate">https://netblue30.github.io/firejail</code> (or<br>
<code class="notranslate">https://firejail.github.io</code> if we want)</li>
</ul>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">It might be better as a separate repo (either by <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/netblue30/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/netblue30">@netblue30</a> or under a firejail<br>
org), as having just a <code class="notranslate">gh-pages</code> branch is not very discoverable IMO.  Also,<br>
this would allow having all PRs relevant to the website in one place, and not<br>
mixed with the PRs intended for a different codebase (i.e.: firejail itself),<br>
which is nicer for organization IMO.</p>
<p dir="auto">Perhaps it could be named something like "firejail-www".  Anyway, I'd just<br>
personally try to avoid using a domain name for it as domain names are not<br>
exactly set in stone and having it differ from the actual website is a bit<br>
